UnitStatement: Verification proves that the software solves the stated mechanics problem correctly within declared tolerances.
Validation evaluates whether the software workflow is fit for its intended engineering support role.
Neither verification nor validation replaces project-specific professional judgment.
This draft is aligned to execution/_Decomposition/SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md revision 0.7 and approved execution/_DAG/DAG-006/ graph coordination authority.

DAG-006 preserves dependency coordination and does not authorize lifecycle changes, release labels, professional approval, legal clearance, certification, sealing, authentication, or code-compliance claims.
The strategy keeps five evidence surfaces separate.
Mechanics verification is benchmark comparison for open mechanics behavior.
Validation evidence covers workflow fitness, reproducibility, warnings, and limitation evidence.
User-rule checks are deterministic computation against user-supplied rule-pack inputs and definitions.
Release quality evidence is software maturity inputs for future release gates.
Professional reliance is competent human review outside automatic software authority.
Units and schemas benchmark family covers dimensional conversions, invalid unit rejection, and schema completeness, with automated tests as required evidence.
Frame mechanics benchmark family covers cantilever, fixed-fixed thermal growth, portal frame, and inclined member transforms, with hand calculations and automated comparisons as required evidence.
Piping loads benchmark family covers weight, pressure thrust where modeled, imposed displacement, and thermal expansion, with hand calculations and regression outputs as required evidence.
Stress recovery benchmark family covers axial, bending, torsion, pressure membrane, and stress range, with hand calculations as required evidence.
Nonlinear supports benchmark family covers one-way support, gap, lift-off, and friction active state, with convergence and state trace as required evidence.
Rule packs benchmark family covers invented demo values, missing required inputs, unit mismatch, and unsafe expression, with evaluator tests as required evidence.
Reports benchmark family covers reproducibility, checksum stability, warning inclusion, and protected-content lint, with report tests as required evidence.
Where benchmark evidence relies on a hand calculation, the source of record is the machine-readable hand-calc witness artifact.
Human-facing Markdown, MathML, PDF, or report excerpts are deterministic renderings from the hand-calc witness for inspection and review.
Automated comparisons, hashes, provenance review, and repeatability checks must bind to the machine-readable witness, not to a manually edited rendering.
The initial mechanics benchmark suite for DEL-09-01 lives under validation/benchmarks/mechanics/ with hand-calculation notes under validation/hand_calcs/mechanics/.
The mechanics benchmark suite required fixture families are cantilever, frame, thermal growth, imposed displacement, and stiffness transform.
The mechanics benchmark fixtures use original invented values and keep final release tolerances, CI gates, and professional reliance policy as TBD until human approval.
The initial stress recovery benchmark suite for DEL-09-02 lives under validation/benchmarks/stress/ with hand-calculation notes under validation/hand_calcs/stress/.
The stress recovery benchmark suite required fixture families are axial normal stress, bending normal stress, torsional shear stress, pressure membrane stress, and mechanics-only stress range.

The stress recovery benchmark fixtures use original invented values and keep final release tolerances, CI gates, fatigue/allowable criteria, and professional reliance policy as TBD until human approval.
The validation manual skeleton lives at docs/validation_manual/index.md.
The validation manual is a draft evidence-organization surface for maintainers and reviewers; it is not an engineering seal, code-compliance ruling, or project-specific reliance record.
The validation manual shall include sections for product scope and limitations, solver theory summary, unit and schema verification, element verification, and load and stress recovery verification.

The validation manual shall include sections for nonlinear support verification, rule-pack evaluator verification, GUI workflow validation, report reproducibility validation, and known limitations and open issues.
Each validation manual section must state whether it is verification evidence, workflow validation evidence, user-rule-check evidence, or professional-reliance context.
Missing evidence, unapproved thresholds, and unresolved source/provenance questions remain explicit TBD items until a governed decision or evidence record exists.
Release quality evidence is distinct from validation evidence and professional reliance.
Until the release-label vocabulary and final release policy are settled by the human project authority, validation evidence may only be used as input to a future release-quality review.
A future release-quality review should record mechanics benchmark status for affected solver behavior.
A future release-quality review should record stress-recovery benchmark status for affected stress/result behavior.
A future release-quality review should record nonlinear support regression status where nonlinear behavior is affected.
A future release-quality review should record rule-pack missing-input, unit, provenance, and sandbox test status where rule behavior is affected.
A future release-quality review should record report reproducibility, checksum, warning, and protected-content lint status where reports, public examples, or templates are affected.
A future release-quality review should record known limitations, unresolved risks, and human-maintainer dispositions.
The final benchmark tolerance policy, public benchmark source acceptance process, release-label policy, GUI validation evidence requirements, and validation evidence-bundle storage format remain TBD.
Validation examples must be original, public-domain, or permissively licensed.
Protected code examples and commercial software examples are not acceptable unless written permission is documented.

Each public mechanics benchmark fixture must record source/provenance, redistribution status, contributor or generator note, assumptions, units, expected result fields, and review disposition before it is treated as accepted public validation evidence.
Each public hand-calc witness must be original, public-domain, or permissively licensed.
Each public hand-calc witness must record units, assumptions, symbolic and numeric steps, expected results, tolerance basis or TBD, provenance, redistribution status, and review disposition.
Any human rendering of a hand-calc witness must be generated deterministically from the machine-readable witness artifact.
Each public stress recovery benchmark fixture must follow the same provenance rule and must remain limited to open mechanics component comparisons.
Stress range fixtures are mechanics differences between result states; they are not fatigue checks, allowable comparisons, code compliance checks, or professional approval records.

The public benchmark source acceptance workflow remains TBD; until settled, source/provenance records are review evidence only and must not be treated as legal clearance or final public benchmark acceptance.

Validation evidence bundles must preserve source artifacts, commands, generated outputs, hashes or checksums where applicable, provenance, review disposition, known limitations, and unresolved TBD items.
The long-term storage location, package format, retention policy, and release attachment workflow for reviewed validation evidence bundles remain TBD.
GUI validation evidence is TBD until GUI workflow deliverables provide the relevant surfaces.

Future GUI evidence should preserve missing-data visibility, warning presentation, analysis-status transitions, accessibility or usability findings where applicable, and screenshots or automated interaction records without making professional-reliance claims.
